claims.claim: AWS Q2 2026 sales grew 37% to $42.2B, its fastest growth in 18 quarters, while Amazon disclosed AI and Chips businesses each above $25B run rates, strengthening evidence of vertically integrated AI infrastructure leverage.

risks.risk: AI infrastructure expansion is exceptionally capital intensive and may compress free cash flow despite strong demand.

unknowns.unknown: Long-run returns on the current AI infrastructure investment wave are not yet observable.

claims.claim: Q2 net sales rose 20% to $200.6B and operating income rose 43% to $27.5B; operating cash flow grew 33% TTM, while TTM free cash flow swung to a $7.6B outflow primarily from $66.1B higher property-and-equipment purchases tied mainly to AI investment.

risks.risk: Free-cash-flow deterioration creates an execution burden: rapid AI growth must ultimately earn adequate returns on sharply higher infrastructure spending.

contradictions.contradiction: Strong operating-income and AWS growth coexist with negative TTM free cash flow because AI capex accelerated materially.

unknowns.unknown: Timing of normalization in AI capex intensity and free cash flow remains unknown.
